name: Favicon cache supercookie (F-CACHE)
plain: A site encodes an ID into which favicons were cached, which survives clearing cookies.
meaning: NDSS 2021 (Solomos et al.) showed a persistent ID stored in the favicon cache across subdomains, surviving cookie clearing and even private browsing in some browsers. Vendors patched after disclosure.

web.api: Favicon requests to N subdomain paths; navigation redirect probing

steps: Load pages with chosen favicons to write bits

limits.headline: Can try to tag your browser with a hidden icon cache ID, though fixes limit it
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when you visit a site that tries it
can: Store an ID using which tiny site icons your browser has cached
Recognise a returning visitor, even after you clear cookies in unpatched browsers
Link visits across subdomains of the same site in older versions
cannot: Work in browsers that fixed it after researchers reported it in 2021
Survive clearing browsing data in updated browsers
limits.differs: Browser makers patched it after 2021, so behavior differs by version.

story.what_it_is: A site hides an ID in which tiny page icons your browser has saved.
story.for_you: You never see it. You clear cookies and history, and a site still knows it is you, because of the pattern of tiny icons your browser saved. Browsers have worked to close this.
story.for_makers: Researchers showed it works across subdomains and even in private mode. A tracker could use it as a persistent ID. Makers who care about privacy prefer to avoid it, and browsers are closing the hole.

use_cases.example: A tracking network sets a pattern of favicons on a first visit and reads it back later to recognize you.
A measurement script reconnects returning visitors who cleared cookies.
A fraud tool uses it to link accounts from one browser even in private windows.
A marketing site recognizes a shopper who tries to look anonymous.
A game site could link a banned user to a new account made in the same browser.
A publisher could count one reader as one person across paywall resets.

technical_bounds: Patched in Chrome, Safari and Brave (reported)

value.abuse: Cookie-free persistent tracking, survives incognito in affected builds

history.change: Solomos et al. Tracking You Persistently via Favicons (NDSS 2021)
